To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the administration of cholesteryamine to digitalized human patients results in an accelerated metabolic disposition of digitotoxin and a more rapid return to baseline values of the cardiac systolic intervals.

cholestyamine treatment of digitalized human subjects results in an accelerated rate of disappearance of serum digitoxin radioactivity, a more rapid return to baseline of digitoxin induced changes in the LV and QS intervals, and a more rapid return of serum digitoxan radioactivity to baseline values, all presumably mediated by interruption in the enteroheptic circulation of digitoxan by cholestyamine.
cholestyamine treatment of digitalized humans accelerates the metabolic clearance of digitoxin, presumably by interrupt the enterohepati circulation of digitoxins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of digitalin and its derivatives, which are used in the treatment of heart disease.
the metabolic disposition of digitalis gly-cosides and the role of the intestinal tract in the metabolism of these compounds.
the metabolic disposition of digitalis glyco-sides in man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enteroheaptic circulation of digitoxins is interrupted by cholestyamine in man and that this results in an accelerated metabolism of the glycosides and a shortened duration of action.

cholestyamine, a nonabsorbable, nonionic, high-molecular-weight anion-exchange resin, binds digitoxin in vitro, accelerates its metabolic disposition in vivo, and interrupts the enteroheptic circulation of the drug.
cholestyamine accelerates the metabolic dispostion of digitalis glycoisdes by interrupting their enterohepatically recirculation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cholestyamine is a potent and effective agent for the interruption of the ente-rohepatic circulation and for the enhancement of the metabolic disposition of digitalis glyco-sides in man.
cholestyamine is a potent inhibitor of the entero-hepatic circulation of digitalis glyco-sides in man and other species, including the rat and guinea pig.
we have shown in the rat that cholestyamine can interrupt the enterohepatocytic cycle of digitoxin, and in the human that it can shorten the half-life of digitoxin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated that the enterohepic cycle of digitoxin exists in man and contributes to the prolonged cardiac action of this glycoside.
cholestyamine, a drug that is commonly used in clinical practice for lowering cholesterol, may be useful in the management of digitalis intoxication.
